clue.text: Sort of blue dog turning over in bed

indicators.note: in tells us the turned dog goes inside the word for bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: turning over means the word for the dog is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: a lab is short for a Labrador dog

explanation.surface: A blue-coloured dog rolls over in its basket.
explanation.walkthrough: A lab is the familiar short name for a Labrador retriever; 'turning over' and 'in' are the two signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobalt blue is a deep pigment shade, so the word names a sort of blue.

clue.text: One slightly altering publicity, showing greater fairness

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a piece of publicity
juster is the comparative of just, fairer

explanation.surface: An advertising agent tweaks a campaign and claims it is now more even-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes small changes to something, like an insurance assessor tuning a claim, is one who adjusts it.

clue.text: Vessel perfectly visible around united part of Europe

indicators.note: around says the phrase for perfectly is wrapped about the next letters

parts.note: to a T means perfectly, exactly
U is a common abbreviation for united, as in football club names
GB, Great Britain, is part of Europe

explanation.surface: A ship is clearly seen near a unified slice of the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: TO A T (perfectly) goes 'around' U and GB; 'visible' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tug is a small powerful boat, a type of vessel used to tow larger ships.

clue.text: Form of identification — one abandoned by S American state

indicators.note: abandoned by says the letter for one is left out of the country's name

parts.note: Suriname is a country on the north coast of South America
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An ID document is left behind by a South American country.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I (one) from SURINAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A family name is the part of your name that identifies you on forms and documents.

clue.text: Tropical palm in areas bordering public park

indicators.note: bordering means the two area letters sit on either side of the park word

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area, so two areas give two A's
a rec is a recreation ground, a British public park

explanation.surface: A palm tree grows in zones around a town park.
explanation.walkthrough: REC, a 'recreation ground' or public playing field in Britain, sits between A and A.
explanation.definitionFit: The areca is a genus of tropical palm, source of the betel nut.

clue.text: Clothing ornament English landlord briefly keeps in French city?

indicators.note: keeps in says the English landlord holds the French city inside
briefly means the word for landlord loses its last letter

parts.note: a letter is one who lets property, a landlord
Pau is a city in south-west France

explanation.surface: A shoulder decoration: an English landlord keeps it in a French town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts LETTER to LETTE; E and LETTE then 'keep in' PAU.
explanation.definitionFit: An epaulette is the decorative shoulder piece on a uniform, an ornament on clothing.

clue.text: Like Greene's man, caught by girl of inferior character?

parts.note: Graham Greene wrote The Third Man, so his man is the third
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Is Graham Greene's hero, trapped by a girl, a bit of a lowlife?
explanation.walkthrough: The Third Man is Graham Greene's story of post-war Vienna.
explanation.definitionFit: Something third-rate or low-grade is of poor quality, so of inferior character.

clue.text: Family member briefly disturbed by current liveliness

indicators.note: disturbed by means the shortened relative is broken into by the current letter
briefly means the family member is shortened to its common short form

parts.note: a brother is a family member, shortened to bro
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A sibling interrupted by a stream of energy becomes spirited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' turns BROTHER into BRO, and 'disturbed by' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is vigour and dash, a synonym for liveliness in performance.

clue.text: Murderer: one kept in jail

indicators.note: kept in says the letter for one is held inside the word for jail

parts.note: the can is slang for prison
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A killer, one locked up in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Cain killed his brother Abel, the first murderer in the Bible.

clue.text: Doctor shot camel, initially outraging childhood chum

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered into a new order
initially means take only the opening letter of outraging

explanation.surface: A vet shoots a camel, appalling the narrator's old friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is an anagram signal on SHOT, CAMEL and O (first of 'outraging').
explanation.definitionFit: A friend from one's school days is a companion from childhood.

clue.text: Plant in holiday venue — ring-shaped, some say

parts.note: a camp, such as a holiday camp, is a holiday venue

indicators.note: some say means the next piece is a word as spoken, matching the sound

parts.note: annular means shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: A plant grows at a holiday camp, ring-shaped, according to some.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent ANNULAR sounds like ANULA.
explanation.definitionFit: Campanula is the bellflower genus, a garden plant with bell-shaped blooms.

clue.text: In small shelter, Republican beginning to saw wood

indicators.note: In says the following letters go inside the word for small shelter

parts.note: a hut is a small shelter

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of saw

explanation.surface: A Republican in a shed starts sawing timber.
explanation.walkthrough: R and S go 'In' HUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurst is an old word for a wooded hill or grove, found in place names.

clue.text: Forbidden to enclose key in informal communication

indicators.note: to enclose says the forbidden phrase wraps around the key letter

parts.note: not let means not allowed, forbidden
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: It is banned to slip a key inside a casual note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forbidden' is a two-word phrase here, and 'to enclose' puts the key letter between its words.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded card for short, informal messages.

clue.text: Person bringing out article rejected by teacher

indicators.note: rejected by says the teacher word throws out the article letter

parts.note: an educator is a teacher
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A grammar point is thrown out by the schoolteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A from EDUCATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An eductor is one who draws or leads something out, from Latin educere, to lead out.

clue.text: Cunning methods for building vaulted passages

parts.note: arch means sly or knowing, so cunning
ways are methods; the ways are also the slipway framework for building ships

explanation.surface: Clever construction techniques produce arched corridors.
explanation.definitionFit: Arched openings or passages beneath a vault are the passages named here.

clue.text: Relative cut by retired writer

indicators.note: retired means the writer word goes back on itself

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument, a writer
to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: A family member is injured by an elderly author.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's son is a family relative.

clue.text: Woman on lorry releasing suppressed emotions

parts.note: Cath is a short form of the woman's name Catherine
an artic is an articulated lorry, a British truck

explanation.surface: A woman riding on a truck lets her pent-up feelings out.
explanation.walkthrough: ARTIC is British for an articulated lorry, a large truck with a separate cab.
explanation.definitionFit: Catharsis is emotional purging, so a cathartic experience lets out bottled feelings.

clue.text: Freight truck that is submerged under spongy ground

indicators.note: submerged under says in this down entry that the abbreviation sits below the ground word

parts.note: a bog is soft, spongy wet ground
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A goods wagon sinks into a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: A bogie is a wheeled undercarriage, and in some regions a low truck for carrying goods.

clue.text: One badly taken in by fat old Italian painter

indicators.note: taken in by says the jumbled letters are held inside the fat word

parts.note: lard is pig fat

indicators.note: badly means the letters of One are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone is poorly fooled by an overweight elderly Italian artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' turns ONE into EONA, which is 'taken in by' LARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci was the great Italian Renaissance artist.

clue.text: Unemotional woman's note about defile on Scottish island

indicators.note: in this down entry, on means the pass sits above the Scottish island
about is used loosely here to send the note to the far side of the pass and island

parts.note: Di is a woman's name, so a woman's gives Di's
a defile is a narrow pass through hills
Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides
te is a note in tonic sol-fa

explanation.surface: A cold woman writes a memo about a mountain gorge on a Hebridean isle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defile' looks like a verb but is a noun, a narrow mountain pass; 'about' is a loose placing signal that puts TE after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispassionate person is calm and detached, free of feeling, so unemotional.

clue.text: Rowdy university game needing fifty in US city

indicators.note: in says the game and fifty letters go inside the abbreviated city

parts.note: NY is New York
RU is rugby union
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A boisterous college sport needs a half-century in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Unruly means disorderly and hard to control, as is a rowdy crowd.

clue.text: Having thrown up flan, Vic leaving station restaurant

indicators.note: thrown up in a down entry means the flan word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a tart is a flan

indicators.note: leaving says the short name Vic departs from the station name

parts.note: Victoria is a major London railway station

explanation.surface: After vomiting a pastry, Vic abandons a station café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown up' gives TRAT; 'leaving' removes VIC from VICTORIA, the London rail terminus, to give TORIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is a simple Italian eating place, a kind of restaurant.

clue.text: Bishop leaves long note welcoming Eastern magistrate

indicators.note: welcoming says the cut note takes the eastern letter inside it
leaves means the bishop's letter departs from the long note

parts.note: a breve is a long musical note
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop departs, sending a lengthy letter inviting an official from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a noun but is the verb: B leaves BREVE, giving REVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local official in medieval England with judicial powers, a magistrate.

clue.text: He has informed foreign nobleman about transport in homeland

indicators.note: has means the word for informed holds He inside

parts.note: told means informed
a count is a continental nobleman, the British equivalent being an earl
RY, railway, is a means of transport

explanation.surface: A man reports that a foreign aristocrat is concerned with travel back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a containment signal, the word for informed holding He; 'about' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Emigrants speak of their native land as the place they left behind.

clue.text: Man with papers, reportedly Greek native?

parts.note: ID is identity papers
IOM is the Isle of Man

indicators.note: reportedly means the next word is heard, not written

parts.note: Attic means of Attica or Athens, so Greek

explanation.surface: Is someone carrying documents, so they say, a born Greek?
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a British crown dependency, IOM for short.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic language is natural to native speakers, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Patent argument in support of Hutton's first run

indicators.note: in a down entry, in support of means the argument word sits underneath

parts.note: patent means obvious, overt

indicators.note: first means just the initial letter of Hutton's

parts.note: a row is an argument

explanation.surface: A clear quarrel in defence of Hutton's opening run in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: Len Hutton was a famous England cricketer; an overthrow is a run scored when a fielder's throw misses the stumps.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an overthrow is an extra run gained from an errant throw.

clue.text: What river lies to south of Jolson's tavern?

indicators.note: in this down entry, lies to south of means the next pieces come below

parts.note: Al Jolson was an American singer, so Jolson's first name is Al
eh is an exclamation like what?
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: Which river runs south of Jolson's bar?
explanation.definitionFit: An alehouse is an old word for a pub, a tavern serving beer.

clue.text: Briefly visit West, lacking experience of life

indicators.note: Briefly means the visiting phrase loses its last letter

parts.note: to call on is to visit

explanation.surface: Pop in to the west for a moment, inexperienced as you are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' cuts CALL ON to CALLO.
explanation.definitionFit: Callow describes a young person who is immature and naive.

clue.text: Tropical plant possessed by Mexican nanny

indicators.note: possessed by means the letters are held within the words Mexican nanny

explanation.surface: A tropical plant belongs to a Mexican childminder.
explanation.definitionFit: Canna is a genus of tropical flowering plant known as Indian shot.

clue.text: Blighter ignoring wit's opening gag

indicators.note: ignoring means the opening letter of wit's is left out

parts.note: a blighter is a wretch, a contemptible person

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of wit's

explanation.surface: A rascal disregards the comedian's opening joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gag' looks like a joke but is the verb, to heave.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag is to choke or heave as though about to vomit.
